note_on_verdict: Erdos 40 asks for the SET of functions g. This campaign pins that set from two sides and reformulates it exactly; it does not identify it.

what_the_source_page_contains.entire_body_of_page: This is a stronger form of the Erdos-Turan conjecture [28] (since establishing this for any function g(N) -> infinity would imply a positive solution to [28]).

semantic_binding.rep_eq_sumConv: rep A n = sum over antidiagonal n of 1_A p.1 * 1_A p.2 -- the object studied IS the upstream sumRep; ordered pairs, diagonal included
semantic_binding.ncard_eq_cnt: (A cap Set.Icc 1 N).ncard = cnt A N -- the counting function IS the upstream one, window [1,N], 0 excluded
semantic_binding.Erdos40For: restated verbatim from upstream with sumRep replaced by the bound rep

reformulation.limsup_eq_top_iff: limsup (rep A n : ENat) = top  <->  r_A is NOT bounded by any B (uniformly on all of N, not merely eventually)
reformulation.erdos40For_iff: Erdos40For g  <->  every A with a BOUNDED representation function fails the density hypothesis (sqrt N / g N) =O cnt A N. This is the exact form in which Erdos 40 is the question of how dense an infinite B2[k] set can be.

answer_set_is_a_down_set.Erdos40For.of_le: g1 <= g2 eventually and g1 > 0 eventually: Erdos40For g2 -> Erdos40For g1. The answer set is DOWNWARD CLOSED in the growth order.

CEILING_upper_pin.not_erdos40For_of_bounded_witness: one set with bounded rep and dominant counting function refutes g
CEILING_upper_pin.IsSidon / rep_le_two_of_isSidon: textbook Sidon definition; a Sidon set has r_A <= 2
CEILING_upper_pin.P2_isSidon: the powers of two are a Sidon set (2^i + 2^a = 2^j + 2^b with 2^a <= 2^i, 2^b <= 2^j forces 2^i = 2^j)
CEILING_upper_pin.log_isBigO_cnt_P2: log N <= log(2) * |P2 cap [1,N]| for N >= 1
CEILING_upper_pin.not_erdos40For_of_thr_isBigO_log: MAIN CEILING: no g whose threshold sqrt(N)/g(N) is O(log N) is an answer
CEILING_upper_pin.not_erdos40For_sqrt_div_log: explicitly, g(N) = sqrt(N)/log N is NOT an answer
CEILING_upper_pin.tendsto_sqrt_div_log_atTop: and that g really does tend to infinity, so the exclusion is of the kind the problem asks about
CEILING_upper_pin.exists_tendsto_atTop_not_erdos40For: hence the answer set is not everything, witnessed by a genuine g -> infinity
CEILING_upper_pin.answer_set_ceiling: contrapositive form: every answer g has threshold NOT dominated by log N
CEILING_upper_pin.not_erdos40For_of_dense_sidon: THE SOCKET: any Sidon set dense enough to dominate the threshold refutes g. Every future improvement in infinite-Sidon-set density lowers this ceiling with no further work.

FLOOR_lower_pin.basis_count: if (A+A) omits only finitely many naturals then there is M with N - M <= (|A cap [1,N]| + 1)^2 for every N
FLOOR_lower_pin.sqrt_le_three_mul_cnt: hence sqrt(N) <= 3 |A cap [1,N]| for all N >= 2M+4
FLOOR_lower_pin.erdos28_of_erdos40For: MAIN FLOOR: a SINGLE g that is eventually >= 1 and lies in the answer set already yields the Erdos-Turan conjecture (Erdos Problem 28, open, $500)
FLOOR_lower_pin.strictly_stronger_than_upstream: upstream erdos_40.variants.implies_erdos_28 assumes Erdos40ForSet Set.univ and instantiates at the trivial g = sqrt(N), where the density hypothesis is vacuous. The banked theorem needs only ONE g and supplies the missing counting bound |A cap [1,N]| >> sqrt(N) for additive bases. It is the source page's own parenthetical remark, kernel-checked.

banked_lean.net_structural_statement: answer_set_trapped: any g in the answer set of Erdos 40 (eventually >= 1) simultaneously settles Erdos-Turan AND has threshold sqrt(N)/g(N) strictly beyond log N. The answer set lies between an open $500 conjecture below and an explicit kernel-checked ceiling above.

numeric_verification.method: brute-force enumeration from the definitions, sharing no code with the Lean development
checks: C1 r_P2(n) <= 2 for all n <= 100000 (max observed 2)
C2 the powers of two are Sidon (no unordered-pair collision)
C4 log N <= log(2) * |P2 cap [1,N]| (the =O constant used in the Lean)
C6 basis counting bound N - M <= (|A cap [1,N]| + 1)^2 on 5 additive bases
C7 sqrt(N) <= 3 |A cap [1,N]| for N >= 2M+4 on the same 5 bases
C8 the max-unique criterion never asserts rep <= 2 where a direct count exceeds 2 (200 random sets)
numeric_verification.transfer_caveat: Per the source page, Erdos 40 cannot be resolved by a finite computation. This run tests the finite lemmas the Lean rests on; it is NOT evidence about the problem itself.

literature_pointers_UNPROVED_here.caveat: NOT verified by any tool in this campaign, NOT formalised, and NOT used in any banked proof. Recorded only as the named route by which the banked ceiling would be lowered. Treat as UNPROVED.

mian_chowla_greedy_sidon.claim: the greedy (Mian-Chowla) infinite Sidon set satisfies a_n = O(n^3), hence |A cap [1,N]| >> N^{1/3}

ruzsa_dense_infinite_sidon.claim: an infinite Sidon set with |A cap [1,N]| >> N^{sqrt(2)-1-o(1)} exists

literature_pointers_UNPROVED_here.how_to_use_them: each plugs directly into the banked Erdos40.not_erdos40For_of_dense_sidon; only the construction and its counting bound need formalising.

gap_to_close.affirmative_side: no g is known to work, and by the banked erdos28_of_erdos40For any single one would settle Erdos-Turan (erdos:28, open, $500). Not narrowed by this campaign.
gap_to_close.negative_side: the answer set is empty iff for every g -> infinity there is a set with bounded representation function and counting function >> sqrt(N)/g(N) -- the dense infinite Sidon set question. The banked ceiling reaches only g >= sqrt(N)/log N, using the crudest possible witness (a lacunary set). Not narrowed beyond that.
gap_to_close.distance: the interesting regime is g growing arbitrarily slowly (log log N, log N). The banked ceiling sits at sqrt(N)/log N, and even the unformalised Ruzsa construction would reach only N^{0.086}. The gap is essentially the whole problem.
